output.one_liner: Sentry is an error tracking and performance monitoring platform providing REST APIs to programmatically manage organizations, teams, projects, and analyze event/issue data.

auth.notes: Bearer tokens (static personal access tokens) created via internal integrations or user settings, and OAuth2 with authorization code grant. All requests use 'Authorization: Bearer {TOKEN}' header.

evidence.snippet: Authentication tokens are passed using an auth header, and are used to authenticate as a user or organization account with the API.
For third-party applications that need to access Sentry on behalf of users, Sentry supports OAuth2 with the authorization code grant type.

access.notes: Free Developer plan available to anyone after 14-day free trial on Business plan; no payment or approval required. Tokens created via internal integrations accessible to any user account.

evidence.snippet: Without a paid plan, you will be automatically assigned a free Developer plan at the end of your trial.
You can create authentication tokens within Sentry by creating an internal integration.

api_surface.rate_limit_note: Fixed window rate limiting per endpoint, plus concurrent request limits. Response headers: X-Sentry-Rate-Limit-Limit, X-Sentry-Rate-Limit-Remaining, X-Sentry-Rate-Limit-Reset, X-Sentry-Rate-Limit-ConcurrentLimit, X-Sentry-Rate-Limit-ConcurrentRemaining. Webhooks recommended over polling.

evidence.snippet: Bulk Mutate Issues, Create Issue View, Get Debug Information, List Events, Retrieve Events, Update Issue
Create New Project, Link Repository, List Client Keys, Register Service Hook, Update Project
Sentry rate limits every API request made to prevent abuse and resource overuse.
Webhooks are a way for two applications or services to communicate over the web, allowing one application to send automatic notifications.

buildability.rationale: Free self-serve credentials, OAuth2 support with Composio-managed option, broad documented REST API, and webhooks available. Composio toolkit already exists with 212 tools.

overview_evidence.snippet: The Sentry web API is used to access the Sentry platform programmatically.
Auth: OAUTH2, Composio-managed OAuth available? Yes, Tools: 212
